articles.title: Why Demon Slayer's Animation Feels So Different
articles.description: How studio ufotable mixes 2D drawings with 3D effects to make fights look like moving paintings.
body: When Demon Slayer first aired in 2019, a lot of people said the same thing: it looks like a movie. Episode 19, where Tanjiro uses Hinokami Kagura for the first time, went viral within hours and many viewers who never watched anime before started the show because of clips of that scene.

The studio behind it, ufotable, is famous for mixing hand drawn characters with digital effects. The water and fire from the breathing styles are inspired by traditional Japanese ukiyo-e art, so even the special effects feel like part of the painting instead of something added on top.

Another reason is camera movement. In many action anime the camera stays still and the characters move. In Demon Slayer the camera spins around the fight, follows the sword and zooms in on faces. This makes you feel like you are standing inside the battle.

Of course, the story helps too. Tanjiro is not a cold hero. He cries, he apologises to demons and he never stops caring about his sister. The beautiful animation gives those emotional moments extra weight.
If you haven't started yet, begin with season one and don't skip the openings - Gurenge by LiSA is part of the experience.
articles.author: Hamza R.

articles.title: Studio Ghibli: Where Should You Start?
articles.description: A simple guide for new fans - which Ghibli film to watch first and why.
body: Studio Ghibli has made some of the most loved animated movies ever, but if you've never watched one it can be hard to choose. Here is our simple starting list.

Spirited Away is the most famous one and won the Oscar for Best Animated Feature. It follows Chihiro, a girl who gets trapped in a world of spirits. It is strange, beautiful and a little scary, which makes it a great first pick.

If you want something lighter, My Neighbor Totoro is perfect for a family movie night. Nothing very dramatic happens, but it feels warm and peaceful. Kiki's Delivery Service is another relaxing choice about a young witch finding her place.
For action fans, Princess Mononoke is the one to watch. It is about the fight between humans and nature and has some intense battle scenes.
Our advice: don't rush. Watch one film a week and you will soon understand why people love these movies so much.
articles.author: Ayesha K.

articles.title: Open Worlds: From Los Santos to the Lands Between
articles.description: How games like GTA, Red Dead and Elden Ring make huge worlds feel alive.
body: A big map alone does not make a good open world game. Some of the biggest games ever have empty worlds that feel boring after a few hours. So what makes the best ones special?

Rockstar's games like GTA V and Red Dead Redemption 2 focus on detail. People walk around with their own routines, shops open and close, and the weather changes how the world feels. You believe the world keeps going even when you are not looking.

Elden Ring takes another approach. It gives very little direction and lets you explore. You see a castle on the horizon and you simply walk there. Finding a hidden cave or a secret boss feels like a real discovery because the game did not mark it on the map.
Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom gives players tools and lets them solve problems their own way. Fans have built flying machines and robots that the developers never expected.
With GTA VI coming, a lot of people are wondering what the next step will be. Our guess: even smarter NPCs and a city that reacts to everything you do.
articles.author: Usman A.

articles.title: Why Minecraft Never Gets Old
articles.description: More than a decade later, the block game is still one of the most played games on the planet.
body: Minecraft came out as a small indie game and became one of the best selling games of all time. Kids who started playing it years ago are now adults who still log in with friends.
The secret is freedom. There is no single way to play. Some people build giant cities, some explore caves, some make complex redstone machines and others just farm and relax.
Minecraft is also used in schools to teach coding, maths and even history. Teachers have recreated old cities so students can walk around them.
Regular free updates keep the game fresh. New mobs, biomes and blocks give old players a reason to come back.
If you want to try it with friends, start a survival world and set one small goal - like building a house before the first night. You'll be hooked.
articles.author: Bilal M.

articles.title: Christopher Nolan and the Magic of Practical Effects
articles.description: Real sets, real explosions and very little green screen - why Nolan's movies feel so real.
body: Christopher Nolan is famous for doing things for real whenever he can. In The Dark Knight a real truck was flipped in the middle of a city street. In Inception a hallway was built that could spin completely so the actors could fight on the walls.

For Interstellar, the team built the spacecraft interiors and projected space outside the windows instead of adding it later with a green screen. The actors could actually see where they were, which helped their performances.
The famous black hole, Gargantua, was created with help from physicist Kip Thorne. The visual effects team used real equations to show how light would bend around it.
Practical effects are expensive and slow, but audiences can feel the difference. Things have weight and light behaves naturally.
If you plan a Nolan marathon, our order is: The Dark Knight, Inception, Interstellar and then Oppenheimer.
articles.author: Sara N.

articles.title: Dune: Bringing an 'Unfilmable' Book to the Screen
articles.description: For years people said Dune could never be adapted well. Denis Villeneuve proved them wrong.
body: Frank Herbert's Dune was published in 1965 and has a huge world full of politics, religion and giant sandworms. Many filmmakers tried to adapt it and many said it was impossible.

Denis Villeneuve decided to split the first book into two movies. This gave the story enough room to breathe. The first film sets up the world and the second focuses on Paul's journey with the Fremen.
The movies use huge desert locations in Jordan and Abu Dhabi, deep sound design and Hans Zimmer's music to make Arrakis feel real and dangerous.
The cast also helped a lot. Timothee Chalamet, Zendaya, Rebecca Ferguson and Austin Butler brought the characters to life.
With Dune: Part Three on the way, fans are excited to see how the story of Paul continues.
articles.author: Ali H.

articles.title: Stranger Things: How 80s Nostalgia Became a Global Hit
articles.description: Bikes, arcades and synth music - how a show about the 1980s won over viewers born decades later.
body: When Stranger Things came out in 2016 nobody expected it to become one of Netflix's biggest shows. It mixed Steven Spielberg adventure, Stephen King horror and a group of friends on bikes.
The show uses 80s music, clothes and toys to create a strong mood. Songs like Kate Bush's Running Up That Hill became hits again because of the show, decades after they first came out.
But nostalgia alone does not keep people watching for years. The real heart of the show is the friendship between Eleven, Mike, Dustin, Lucas and Will. Viewers literally watched the cast grow up.
The monsters from the Upside Down, like the Demogorgon and Vecna, also gave fans endless theories to discuss online.
Now that the story has ended, fans are rewatching from season one to catch all the clues they missed.
articles.author: Hira S.

articles.title: Why We Still Talk About Game of Thrones
articles.description: Years after the finale, Game of Thrones is still the show everyone compares new fantasy series to.
body: Game of Thrones changed TV. It showed that a fantasy show could have movie-level battles and serious political drama at the same time.
One reason people remember it is that no character was safe. When Ned Stark died in season one, viewers realised this was not a normal show.
The final season divided fans a lot, and people still argue about it. But even the arguments show how much people cared.
House of the Dragon brought many fans back to Westeros and proved there is still interest in this world.
If you never watched it, the first four seasons are some of the best TV ever made.
articles.author: Faraz Q.

articles.title: How K-Pop Choreography Went Global
articles.description: Point choreography, dance challenges and fan covers - the dancing is a huge part of K-Pop's success.
body: In K-Pop, the dance is just as important as the song. Groups practise for months so that every member moves perfectly in sync.
Many songs have a 'point choreography' - a simple, catchy move that fans can copy easily. Think of TWICE's TT pose or PSY's Gangnam Style horse dance.
Social media turned this into dance challenges. Idols post short clips of their new dance and fans all around the world copy it within days.
Dance cover teams are now common in Pakistan too. Groups in Karachi, Lahore and Islamabad practise in parks and malls and perform at fan events.
Want to start? Choose an easy song, slow the video down and practise with a mirror. Most importantly, have fun!
articles.author: Mahnoor T.

articles.title: A Beginner's Guide to K-Pop Fandom Culture
articles.description: Lightsticks, fan chants, comebacks and photocards - a simple guide to the words you'll hear.
body: If you're new to K-Pop you'll hear a lot of new words. Here are the basics.
A 'comeback' is when a group releases new music, not when they return after a break. Each group also has a fandom name - BTS fans are ARMY, BLACKPINK fans are BLINK and TWICE fans are ONCE.
Lightsticks are official glowing sticks for each group. At concerts they are synced so the whole stadium changes colour together.
Fan chants are shouted by fans during specific parts of a song, usually the members' names. Fans learn them before concerts.
Photocards are small photos of members that come inside albums. Many fans collect and trade them - which is why photocard binders are so popular.
articles.author: Zara I.

articles.title: Why Spider-Verse Changed Animated Superhero Films
articles.description: Comic book dots, different art styles in one movie and a hero anyone can relate to.
body: Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse came out in 2018 and looked like nothing else. It used comic book dots, speech boxes and frame rates that make it feel like a moving comic.
Each Spider-person has their own art style. Spider-Man Noir is black and white, Peni Parker looks like an anime character and Spider-Ham looks like an old cartoon.
Across the Spider-Verse went even further with whole worlds drawn in completely different styles, like watercolour for Gwen's universe.
But the story is what makes it great. Miles Morales is a normal teenager who doubts himself. The message 'anyone can wear the mask' connected with people everywhere.
After these movies, many other studios started trying more creative animation styles.
articles.author: Hamza R.

articles.title: Batman: More Than 85 Years of the Dark Knight
articles.description: From 1939 comics to The Batman - why Bruce Wayne keeps coming back.
body: Batman first appeared in Detective Comics #27 in 1939. More than 85 years later he is still one of the most popular heroes in the world.
Part of his appeal is that he has no superpowers. Anyone could, in theory, train hard and become Batman. He relies on his mind, his gadgets and his detective skills.
He also has the best villains. The Joker, Riddler, Catwoman, Two-Face and Penguin are all famous on their own.
Every generation gets its own Batman - Adam West, Michael Keaton, Christian Bale, Ben Affleck and Robert Pattinson all played him differently.
If you want to read the comics, Batman: Year One and The Long Halloween are great places to start.
articles.author: Usman A.

articles.title: Manga vs Anime: Which Should You Start With?
articles.description: Reading or watching? We compare both so you can decide.
body: A lot of new fans ask the same question: should I read the manga or watch the anime first? The honest answer is - it depends on you.
Manga is usually ahead of the anime in story, so readers get to see what happens next. It is also faster - you can read in an hour what the anime shows over several episodes.
Anime adds music, voice acting and colour. Some fights, like in Jujutsu Kaisen or Demon Slayer, become much more exciting when animated.
Our tip: watch the first season of the anime. If you love it and can't wait, continue in the manga from where the anime stops.
Remember to support official releases through apps like Manga Plus or buying volumes from local bookstores.
articles.author: Ayesha K.

articles.title: How One Piece Stays Fresh After So Many Years
articles.description: Eiichiro Oda started One Piece in 1997. Here's why it is still one of the biggest manga in the world.
body: One Piece started in Weekly Shonen Jump in 1997 and it is still running. It is one of the best selling comics in history.
The world keeps growing. Every new island has its own culture, problems and characters, so the story never feels stuck in one place.
Oda also plans clues years in advance. Small details in early chapters turn out to be important hundreds of chapters later, which makes fans love making theories.
The Netflix live action series introduced One Piece to a new audience who had never read manga before.
It looks long, but many fans say the journey is worth it. Start from chapter one and enjoy the ride.
articles.author: Bilal M.

characters.name: Tanjiro Kamado
characters.biography: A kind-hearted boy who becomes a demon slayer after his family is attacked. He travels with his sister Nezuko, who was turned into a demon, and searches for a way to make her human again.

characters.name: Nezuko Kamado
characters.biography: Tanjiro's younger sister who was turned into a demon but still protects humans. She sleeps a lot to regain strength and fights with powerful kicks and blood demon art.

characters.name: Eren Yeager
characters.biography: A boy who swore to destroy every Titan after his hometown was attacked. He later discovers he can turn into a Titan himself, which changes everything he believes.

characters.name: Levi Ackerman
characters.biography: Captain of the Survey Corps special operations squad and known as humanity's strongest soldier. Cold on the outside but deeply cares about his team.

characters.name: Chihiro Ogino
characters.biography: A ten year old girl who gets trapped in the spirit world. She starts off scared and whiny but grows brave while working in a bathhouse to save her parents.

characters.name: Kirito
characters.biography: A solo gamer trapped inside the virtual world of Sword Art Online. He fights with two swords and tries to clear the game so all players can escape.

characters.name: Geralt of Rivia
characters.biography: A monster hunter with white hair, cat-like eyes and two swords - steel for humans, silver for monsters. He looks cold but always helps people in trouble.

characters.name: Arthur Morgan
characters.biography: A senior member of the Van der Linde gang. As the Wild West comes to an end, Arthur starts questioning his loyalty and what kind of man he wants to be.

characters.name: Kratos
characters.biography: The former Greek god of war now lives in the Norse lands with his son Atreus. He is trying to control his anger and be a better father.

characters.name: Link
characters.biography: The silent hero of Hyrule who always returns to fight evil and protect Princess Zelda. Known for his green tunic, Master Sword and love for exploring.

characters.name: V
characters.biography: A mercenary in Night City who gets a digital ghost of rockstar Johnny Silverhand stuck in their head. Players decide V's look, background and choices.

characters.name: Lucia
characters.biography: One of the two main characters of GTA VI, shown in the first trailer. Along with her partner Jason, she gets pulled into crime in the state of Leonida.

characters.name: Paul Atreides
characters.biography: Son of Duke Leto who moves to the desert planet Arrakis. After his family is betrayed, he joins the Fremen and becomes a leader many believe is a messiah.

characters.name: Cooper
characters.biography: A former NASA pilot turned farmer who leaves his children behind to find a new home for humanity through a wormhole near Saturn.

characters.name: Tony Stark
characters.biography: Genius billionaire who built the Iron Man suit. His journey from selfish weapons maker to hero is the backbone of the Marvel movies.

characters.name: Harry Potter
characters.biography: The boy who lived. Harry grows up at Hogwarts with Ron and Hermione and faces Lord Voldemort in the final battle.

characters.name: Dom Cobb
characters.biography: A skilled thief who steals secrets from people's dreams. He takes one last job - planting an idea - so he can go home to his kids.

characters.name: Jake Sully
characters.biography: A former marine who joined the Na'vi of Pandora. In The Way of Water he must protect his family and move to the ocean clans.

characters.name: Eleven
characters.biography: A girl with psychic powers who escaped from Hawkins Lab. She loves Eggos, her friends and her adopted dad Hopper.

characters.name: Wednesday Addams
characters.biography: A sharp and dark-humoured student at Nevermore Academy who investigates a string of murders while trying to control her psychic visions.

characters.name: Jon Snow
characters.franchise: A Song of Ice and Fire
characters.biography: Raised as the bastard son of Ned Stark, Jon joins the Night's Watch and becomes a leader in the war against the White Walkers.

characters.franchise: A Song of Ice and Fire
characters.biography: The Mother of Dragons who wants to take back the Iron Throne. Her journey is one of the most talked about in TV history.

characters.name: Walter White
characters.biography: A chemistry teacher who turns to crime and becomes the feared 'Heisenberg'. A classic example of a hero turning into a villain.

characters.name: Joel Miller
characters.biography: A tough survivor who is hired to smuggle a teenager named Ellie across a ruined America. Slowly she becomes like a daughter to him.

characters.name: RM
characters.biography: Leader and main rapper of BTS. Known for his English speeches, his love for art and nature, and his work as a songwriter and producer.

characters.name: Jungkook
characters.biography: The youngest member of BTS and a main vocalist. Also known for strong dancing and solo hits like 'Seven'.

characters.name: Jennie
characters.biography: Rapper and vocalist of BLACKPINK. She was the first member to go solo with the song 'SOLO' in 2018 and is a big fashion icon.

characters.name: Lisa
characters.biography: Main dancer and rapper of BLACKPINK, originally from Thailand. Her solo song 'Money' became a huge dance challenge.

characters.name: Nayeon
characters.biography: Lead vocalist of TWICE and the first member to debut solo with the bright summer song 'POP!'.

characters.name: Bang Chan
characters.biography: Leader of Stray Kids and part of the producing team 3RACHA. Fans love his late night live streams where he chats with them.

characters.name: Peter Parker / Spider-Man
characters.biography: A teenager from Queens bitten by a radioactive spider. With great power comes great responsibility - he tries to balance school, friends and saving the city.

characters.name: Miles Morales
characters.biography: A Brooklyn teen who becomes Spider-Man in his own universe. He has venom blasts and camouflage powers that Peter doesn't have.

characters.name: Batman
characters.biography: Bruce Wayne watched his parents die and swore to fight crime in Gotham. He has no superpowers, just training, gadgets and detective skills.

characters.name: The Joker
characters.biography: Batman's most famous enemy. A chaotic criminal who treats crime as a joke and loves to prove that anyone can break.

characters.name: Superman
characters.biography: Clark Kent was sent to Earth from the dying planet Krypton. He can fly, has super strength and always tries to do the right thing.

characters.name: Deadpool
characters.biography: Wade Wilson is a mercenary with a healing factor and a big mouth. He breaks the fourth wall and talks directly to the readers.

characters.name: Monkey D. Luffy
characters.biography: Captain of the Straw Hat Pirates. After eating the Gum-Gum Fruit his body stretches like rubber. His dream is to become King of the Pirates.

characters.name: Light Yagami
characters.biography: A top student who finds the Death Note and decides to 'clean' the world of criminals, calling himself Kira.

characters.name: L
characters.biography: The world's greatest detective who sits in strange ways and eats a lot of sweets. He is the only one who can match Light's mind.

characters.name: Denji
characters.biography: A poor young man who merges with his chainsaw devil dog Pochita. He becomes a devil hunter mostly because he wants a normal life and good food.

characters.name: Yuji Itadori
characters.biography: A high school student with crazy strength who eats a cursed finger and becomes the host of Sukuna, the King of Curses.

characters.name: Anya Forger
characters.biography: A little girl who can read minds. She is adopted by a spy and an assassin and loves peanuts and spy cartoons.

characters.name: Naruto Uzumaki
characters.biography: A loud ninja with the Nine-Tailed Fox sealed inside him. Nobody believed in him at first, but he never gave up on his dream of becoming Hokage.
